criterion: The records it parses are limited to the repository it was asked about, and the answer is unchanged for every case the existing tests cover
summary: previous_bypass now reads journal.read_repo(repo) instead of journal.read(), and the in-loop 'entry.get("repo") != repo' skip is removed because every record it consulted already passed that test - so the filtered history is the same records in the same relative order, and the one index space the function depends on is preserved. All 83 tests in tests.test_session_hook_contract pass unchanged, including test_a_session_in_another_repository_is_not_reported, test_a_bypass_already_reported_is_skipped_and_an_older_one_is_found, test_a_question_session_afterwards_does_not_bury_a_bypass and test_two_starts_at_once_report_one_bypass_between_them. Full suite: 395 tests OK on 3.12.12 (skipped=2) and 395 OK on 3.10.19 (skipped=4); black and mypy clean. Measured on a synthetic journal of 40,000 records across 50 repositories (13.1 MB): read()+filter 0.084s vs read_repo() 0.014s, a 6.1x reduction, with the two readers asserted to return identical record lists.
